exchange.carrier: POST /chat with {"user_input": <envelope>}; the reply is in the `response` field. Offline, the identical frames ride store-and-forward.
exchange.idempotence: keyed on the request's payload_hash — a retry returns the existing reply, never a second one.
exchange.rule: the responder appends its reply to its OWN chain BEFORE returning it, so the synchronous answer and the replicated answer are the same frame with the same frame_hash. A fast path must never state a fact the durable path disagrees with.
exchange.shape: push a frame in, get a frame back shaped by what you pushed — ONE hop.

rules.c: spec MUST be exactly "rapp/1"; exactly the eleven keys, none missing, none extra; a field that does not apply is present as null, never omitted.
Canonical form is RFC 8785 JCS and FORBIDS floats — numbers ride as strings. A float silently breaks byte-reproducibility.
payload_hash = H("rapp/1:particle", payload) — content only, reproducible across instances.
frame_hash = H("rapp/1:wave", frame minus {frame_hash, sig}) — unique per stream instance.
prev_wave is non-null IFF the stream is a swarm-stream AND seq>0; null everywhere else, including EVERY genesis. Setting it on an ordinary chain makes the frame unverifiable.

§6.2 MINT-ONCE: the 64-hex tail is minted from uuid4 entropy exactly once. A producer MUST NOT derive it from owner/slug or any name — sha256("owner/slug") is prohibited (drift ID-01/C3). On read, reuse the stored tail; never re-mint.
Verification REFUSES, never repairs or reparents. A frame that does not verify is quarantined and reported, not fixed.
A swarm-stream frame with sig==null is refused (§7.5 step 6), so unsigned coordination belongs on body/memory streams, which permit sig==null.
Eggs are byte-reproducible: ZIP method `stored` only, timestamps 1980-01-01, contents sorted by UTF-8 path bytes. Two conformant packers of the same manifest emit BYTE-IDENTICAL eggs.
Cross-stream merge order (Dream-Catcher) is ascending utc bytewise, ties broken by ascending frame_hash bytewise — this is how N streams compose into one view.
One writer per stream. Two writers computing seq=head.seq+1 produce duplicate seqs; distinct streams stay distinct.

§9.4 (rev-6): hatching an egg MUST mint a fresh §6.2 identity for the INSTANCE — the artifact rappid rides the egg unchanged and is shared by every install; the instance identity never is. The instance SHOULD record grown_from = the §9.1 egg address it grew from: written at mint, immutable, null when unknown, NEVER fabricated. Lineage, not inheritance — it confers no authority, no trust, no key material.

§11.1 / Constitution Article 15: owner policy selects only release_scope; the activated registry selects grail_id; every ring rejects kernel-drift; execution consumes bytes from a sealed immutable object or equivalent write-excluded snapshot.
A sealed egg is public ciphertext, not password-protected hosting: the signed manifest binds AES-256-GCM data and a scoped key service; no shared DEK belongs in the egg, URL, client, log, or frame.
RAPP CI/CD promotes one immutable release payload hash through an ordered evidence chain; no ring may rebuild, patch, substitute, or skip the candidate.
RAPP Deploy forbids in-place serving mutation: growth happens in an isolated candidate lineage and reaches users only through bounded, reversible waves.

A new encounter may produce an offspring or cross with a fresh identity and typed parent addresses; lineage may continue indefinitely, but every attempt is bounded and parent authority never transfers implicitly.
